title: The Crucifixion
lead: Crucifixion was the Roman death for slaves and rebels. The Gospels tell how Jesus was crucified outside Jerusalem, and they tell it in the words of the Psalms and the Prophets, above all Psalm 22.

sections.b: Persians, Carthaginians and Romans executed people by fastening them to a stake or cross and leaving them to die slowly in public. Rome used it for slaves, rebels and the worst criminals; Roman citizens were normally spared it. The law of Moses had a different practice: the body of an executed man could be hung on a tree, but had to be taken down before night, because "a man who is hanged is cursed by God" (Deuteronomy 21:22–23), a verse Paul applies to Jesus (Galatians 3:13).

The four Gospels tell the crucifixion briefly and without dwelling on the pain. Instead they tie it again and again to the Scriptures: Psalm 22 (the cry "My God, my God", the mockers, the clothes divided by lot), Psalm 69 (the sour wine), Psalm 31 ("into your hand"), Isaiah 53 (counted among the rebels), Zechariah 12:10 ("they will look on the one they pierced") and Exodus 12:46 (no bone broken). The early Christians read these passages as showing that the cross was part of God's plan, not a defeat.
sections.refs: Mark 15:21–41; Matthew 27:32–56; Luke 23:26–49; John 19:16–37; Psalm 22:1–31; Psalm 69:21; Isaiah 53:12; Zechariah 12:10
